PullRequest.Title: Keep each window's idle sash grippers its own
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:

Fixes the sash grippers of an auxiliary window of the Agents window disappearing for good while the mouse moves only in that window.

The three-dot sash grippers recede after the mouse has been idle in a window (`workbench.sash.autoHideGrippers`, 2s), and come back on the next mouse move in that window. Two defects broke this for auxiliary windows:

1. **The idle state was mirrored from the main window.** The auxiliary window service mirrors the class attribute of the main window's container onto each auxiliary window's container, on every change. The idle state was a class on that container (`sash-grippers-hidden`). While the mouse moves only in an auxiliary window, the main window goes idle, and its hidden state is copied into the auxiliary window. The idle state is now an attribute of each window's own container (`data-sash-grippers-hidden`), which is not mirrored; the core rule is `.monaco-workbench[data-sash-grippers-hidden] .monaco-sash`. The body and `<html>` are mirrored in full, so the state can't move there either.
2. **The Agents window never added auxiliary window containers.** Its workbench declares `onDidAddContainer` but never fired it, so `SashGrippersController`, and anything else that tracks every container, never tracked an auxiliary window opened after startup. It now fires it for every auxiliary window, as the standard workbench's layout does.

Together, an auxiliary window of the Agents window, such as an editor window, kept its grippers hidden while it was used, until the mouse moved in the main window again. This is a latent bug for any Agents window auxiliary window, and the cause of missing grippers in chat windows (behind `sessions.chatWindows.enabled`, #344666). The standard workbench's main window behaves as before.

## How to test

1. In the Agents window, open an auxiliary window, move the mouse once in the main window, then only in the auxiliary window for a few seconds: its grippers stay. Stop moving: they recede after 2s, and come back on the next move.
2. In a regular window: move the mouse, then stop for 2s: the grippers recede, and come back on the next move.

## Validation

- New tests, both failing without the fix:
  - `Sash grippers`: an auxiliary window keeps its own idle state while it mirrors the class of the main window's container.
  - `Sessions - Workbench`: adds the container of each auxiliary window that opens, and releases it with the window.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/sash/test/browser/sash.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/webview/test/browser/webviewElement.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/test/browser/sessionGridLayout.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/test/browser/workbench.test.ts`: 240 passing.
- `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob "vs/sessions/**/*.test.js"`: 9732 passing, 0 failing.
- `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob "vs/workbench/**/*.test.js"`: 28769 passing, 1 failing (`ChatListWidget` "falls back to a full refresh when the request or the transcript changes", which also fails on `main`).
- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed. `pnpm run eslint <changed files>`: passed.
- Live (background, dev build), with `window.density.layout: compact` and `workbench.editor.showTabs: single`:
  - before: main idle, the mouse moving only in an auxiliary window of the Agents window: that window's container carried the hidden state and its grippers had opacity 0;
  - after: the same scenario: its grippers stay at opacity 1; it recedes after its own 2s idle and returns on its own mouse move;
  - regular workbench: recedes after 2s idle (`--sash-grip-opacity: 0` on every sash) and returns on the next move, as before.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agents workbench startup initializes layout and subscribes for future auxiliary-window containers
Scenarios.CriticalPath: initLayout synchronously creates one event subscription. Accessing IAuxiliaryWindowService does not newly pull a delayed service onto startup in practice because SessionsTabStyleContribution already injects it at WorkbenchPhase.BlockStartup; no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network operation is added.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant work per workbench instance: one listener and one registered disposable.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No concurrent work; subscription setup is synchronous and happens once.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache or cache key participates; cold and warm startup have the same constant registration work.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: initLayout, the delayed service constructor, and BlockStartup contribution injection were traced directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact instantiation ordering can vary by contribution startup, but the service constructor is itself allocation-only and the changed code adds only a listener.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression: the diff adds O(1) startup work and does not introduce an expensive boundary or heavyweight eager initialization.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening and closing an auxiliary editor/chat window in the Agents workbench
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The pre-existing auxiliary-window service creates and registers the window, then synchronously fires onDidOpenAuxiliaryWindow before open() returns. The diff adds an onDidAddContainer notification on that path; current consumers perform a fixed number of class/attribute updates and register per-window DOM listeners. Closing the window disposes the parent event store, nested container store, timeout, and listeners.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create/open an auxiliary browser or native window
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One pre-existing window-open operation per user-requested auxiliary window; the changed event does not add or repeat it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The Agents workbench used the same auxiliary-window creation path but did not notify ILayoutService consumers about the new container.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Window creation remains the dominant pre-existing boundary before the open promise resolves; the changed fixed DOM/listener setup runs after creation and before return.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One notification per auxiliary window open; retained listeners and one idle timer scale linearly with concurrently open windows, the intended ownership model. Current event fan-out is a small fixed set of consumers, not per editor or per DOM row.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Window opens are not burst-scheduled by this change. Each synchronous event completes during its own open path; each open window owns at most one sash idle timeout.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved. Existing windows are discovered through layoutService.containers by late-created contributions, while future windows are delivered once by the event, avoiding duplicate registration.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: event firing order, all repository onDidAddContainer consumers, and disposal ownership were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact cost of fixed consumer DOM updates depends on enabled contributions, but cardinality is one per opened window and no collection-wide relayout or external call is reached by the event handlers.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: fixed per-window bookkeeping is required for correct tracking, is cleaned up on close, and does not amplify the existing window-open boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Mouse activity and two-second idle transitions independently hide sash grippers in each main or auxiliary window
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A distinct mouse position clears/replaces one timeout and removes one container attribute; idle expiry sets the attribute. CSS invalidation is scoped to .monaco-sash descendants in that window. Repeated identical webview coordinates are deduplicated. No external boundary lies on the input or timer path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: JavaScript work is O(1) per distinct mouse event per window; selector matching/style updates scale with the sashes in only that container. At most one timeout is live per tracked window.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Independent windows can each have one pending timer; events are serialized on their window event loops and no unbounded tasks are queued.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved. lastMousePosition serves as per-window event deduplication and remains unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: mouse listener, timeout replacement, attribute mutation, CSS selector scope, and class-only auxiliary mirroring were directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Browser style invalidation cost varies with sash count, but the selector scope and mutation frequency are equivalent to the prior class-based rule and avoid mirroring the main window's idle mutation into auxiliary containers.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression: class-to-attribute replacement preserves local style work and can reduce cross-window invalidation by preventing idle state mirroring.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all seven changed files and every diff page. Traced startup, auxiliary-window open/close ownership, all onDidAddContainer consumers, mouse input, timers, CSS invalidation, service instantiation, and external-boundary cardinality. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance issue or qualifying regression fix was found.
